edit.description: `reserved_node` (:1726) is the tree's one classifier for which species a `Node` is — a leaf under the reserved `EMBEDDED_LEAF_KIND` (:1695), a bare requirement name under `REQUIREMENT_KIND` (:1687), otherwise a member whose `.0` really is its kind — and it answers `Option<&str>`, so every consumer re-compares that answer against a kind constant to learn *which* reserved node it holds (`dangling_mention`, :2287). Give the classification a shape a consumer matches exhaustively instead: a species enum (`Member`/`Requirement`/`EmbeddedLeaf`) returned by a `pub(crate)` accessor over the same grammar reads (`parse_nested_address` first, exactly as today — a corpus kind *named* `requirement` or `embedded` carries its whole address as its id and is a member), with `render_node` (:2272) and `dangling_mention`'s `resolves_against` branch reading it rather than string-comparing. `pub(crate)`, not `pub`: `read` is the one out-of-module consumer and an export earns its consumer (`specs/process/engineering.md`). Behaviour-identical on this side — the two spellings a node renders as do not move.

`why_one` renders a node five times as "`{id}` ({kind})" straight off `node.0` (:1276 outgoing, :1287 contains, :1299 dangling mentions, :1327 incoming, :1335 contained-by), and `node.0` is not a kind for either reserved node. :1303 holds the partial copy of the classifier — `to_kind == graph::REQUIREMENT_KIND && nested_key(to_id).is_none()`, the requirement half only — so a requirement target reads "requirement `ghost-req`" while an embedded leaf reads "`a/b/c/d` (embedded)", naming as a kind the one marker `EMBEDDED_LEAF_KIND`'s own doc calls distinct from every artifact kind. Retire that branch onto the graph-side species match at all five sites, and give the leaf the species voice `specs/model/contract.md` ("Read verbs") already enumerates — explain narrates "a member, requirement, kind, or leaf" — parallel to the existing requirement wording. A member's spelling stays byte-identical.

The pins that would have caught it, in the existing `mention_narration` module (:557) whose `mention_edges` helper (:569) lifts a row through the real `resolved_mention_edges`: a dangling mention whose target is a leaf address narrates the leaf as a leaf and never `(embedded)`; a mention whose *source* is a leaf address (`style/hook/on-enter/command`) narrates the same way on the incoming side. The member and requirement cases are the other half of the pin — `:598`'s "points at `standards` (skill)" and the dangling requirement wording must stay byte-identical, which is what proves the fold moved no spelling it should not have.

Fence allowance, no edit expected: the graph-side call sites the species enum reshapes are the ones this file's mention pins cover (`embedded_edge_targets`, the `dangling_mention`/`ambiguous_mention` families). They must stay green unedited — a message that moves here means the refactor changed a finding's spelling, which is out of scope.

Fence allowance, no edit expected: `:2938` pins `why`'s member wording ("it points at `rust` (rule) via its `mention` field") through the same five render sites. It must stay byte-identical — the member spelling is the branch this entry does not touch.

summary: `explain` names an embedded leaf `(embedded)` as if it were a kind: the node-species classification has two homes and read.rs holds the partial copy.

per.section: A shared concept is one type

tests.asserts: a dangling mention to a leaf address, and a mention from a leaf address, each narrate the leaf as a leaf and never as a member of kind `embedded`; the member and requirement wordings are unchanged

acceptance: `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` green, with `rg 'REQUIREMENT_KIND' src/read.rs` empty (no second copy of the classifier outside `src/graph.rs`) and the two new leaf-narration pins passing.
notes: Measured this tick against a probe harness (one rule, two mention rows): `explain style` printed "it mentions `a/b/c/d` (embedded)" and, with the leaf as the mention source, "`style/hook/on-enter/command` (embedded) points at it". The SDK writes exactly those source rows off a `blocks()` body (`embeddedLeafMentionRows`, `sdk/src/declarations.ts:685`). No test pins either wording today. scoped at 71b89c5e
